title: Beyond the 956: Couple Arrested Pushing Laundry Cart With $1.5 Million in Cash in Manhattan; $3 Million, Drugs and Four Guns Seized
excerpt: John Morales and Amya Douglas, 21, were arrested in Manhattan after agents allegedly caught them pushing a laundry cart loaded with about $1.5 million in cash; a search of their apartment brought the total seized to about $3 million, plus suspected narcotics and four guns.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A New York couple was arrested after federal agents allegedly caught them pushing a laundry cart loaded with about $1.5 million in cash down a Manhattan sidewalk, authorities said.

John Morales and Amya Douglas, 21, were stopped Monday afternoon, November 16, 2026, near 144th Street and Riverside Drive in Manhattan after agents with the Drug Enforcement Administration's New Jersey Field Division allegedly saw them leave an apartment at 670 Riverside Drive pushing the cart toward a double-parked Honda Pilot, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration and the New York City Special Narcotics Prosecutor.

Inside the cart were reusable shopping bags that allegedly turned out to be stuffed with bundles of cash totaling about $1.5 million. Agents had the couple under surveillance as part of an alleged drug-trafficking investigation, prosecutors said.

After obtaining a court-authorized search warrant, agents searched the apartment and allegedly found another roughly $1.5 million in bundled cash, bringing the total seized to about $3 million in alleged narcotics proceeds. Agents also allegedly found about four kilograms — more than eight pounds — of substances believed to include cocaine, heroin and fentanyl pills, along with a money counter and a scale.

In the apartment's front closet, agents allegedly found four guns hidden inside a hollow speaker: a 9 mm pistol, a .22-caliber pistol, a .45-caliber pistol and a .38-caliber revolver, plus ammunition for three of the guns, authorities said.

Morales and Douglas were charged with criminal possession of a controlled substance in the first and third degrees, criminal possession of a weapon in the third degree and criminal possession of a firearm. Morales faces an additional charge of criminal possession of a weapon in the second degree. They were arraigned Tuesday, November 17, in Manhattan Criminal Court, where bail was set at $300,000 cash or a $900,000 bond for Morales and $100,000 cash or a $300,000 bond for Douglas.

Morales and Douglas are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post; U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration press release, “$3 Million Cash, Over Eight Pounds of Narcotics, and Four Guns Seized,” Nov. 18, 2026; New York Post, Nov. 18, 2026.
